observation.visible_scene: A dim workshop scene shot from a fixed camera. A gray cast-metal part (with a yellow sticker) rests on two small wooden blocks on a concrete floor; a spring-type ground clamp with a black cable is hooked onto the part. A person wearing brown leather welding gloves holds a welding torch with a copper contact tip near the part. Background shows a white tarp, dark table legs, and the corner of a machine at top right. A worn sneaker is visible at the left edge throughout.
visible_changes: At t≈0.67–0.83 s an electric arc strikes where the torch tip meets the metal part, creating a bright blue-white flash and a shower of orange sparks that fly left and upward and settle as glowing embers on the floor.
After the arc stops, a small orange-red glow persists at the contact point on the part through roughly t=1.4–2.4 s, then fades.
The gloved hands reposition the torch: it starts held near-horizontally, tip aimed at the part's left side, and by the later frames is held more vertically with the tip near the part's top edge.

Scattered sparks/embers on the floor at the left flicker, fade, and reappear intermittently across the clip; the initial floor sparks in frame 1 indicate a spark-producing action already underway before this segment.
The workpiece, wooden blocks, ground clamp, shoe, and background remain in fixed screen positions; no camera movement is evident.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the floor sparks seen in frame 1 belong to an earlier arc strike outside this crop, and whether the welding continues after the segment ends.
The overall goal or completion of the weld bead.
What the metal part is and what the machine at top right does.
uncertain_details: The exact welding process and the material identity of the part.
Whether the lingering orange glow is an active weld pool or just residual heat.
The precise reason for the torch repositioning (re-striking an arc vs. moving away).
